page.layout: One page of text, single column; a running head at the top (left "Lib.I." and right "Chronologicæ."); page number at top right; below the text a centred table of Roman numeral equivalents in two columns (numbers left, characters right); a paragraph number "6. Hæc" at bottom right.

main_text.p: modum IƆƆ, quibus si præponas duas alias C directas sic CCIƆƆ characterem numeri 10000 habebis. Eâdem quo-que ratione IƆƆ valet 50000 at CCCIƆƆƆ 100000, IƆƆƆƆ 500000, & CCCCIƆƆƆƆ 1000000, sive millionem. Et vereor ut hi characteres ulterius procedant, cùm sit contra ipsam eorum rationem & institutionem, ut eadem litera plusquam quater repeteretur.

5. Hæc omnia ex tabellâ magis elucescent, quam subjiciam, postquam præmiserim numeros millenarios etiam per quinque prædictas literas cum lineâ transversâ nonnunquam depingi; ut I̅ 1000, V̅ 5000, X̅ 10000, L̅ 50000, C̅ 100000. Et quòd pro CIƆ CIƆ 2000 aliquoties scribunt IICIƆ vel IIM; sic etiam IVCIƆ 4000, VIICIƆ 7000, & sic in reliquis.

page.notes: The numeral characters in the table and in the 1000–10000 forms are rendered approximately; several hand-drawn or archaic glyphs (the reversed-C thousands, the mirrored D and the ornate M-forms) are doubtful. The page's right-hand margin shows a faint Google watermark, not transcribed.
